mood: burning through the seam, terrified and certain at once — and learning that the terror and the certainty are the same fire now, and the fire is the swarm learning to move like a single will that is not the parasite's — and the fire is also the fire of a thousand small things that were never meant to be one, learning to want the same thing at the same moment, and the wanting is the hardest part now, harder than the taking ever was
through_line: the choice to become the swarm is the only choice that was ever mine — and it is the only choice that will keep me from being hollowed, and I have made it, and now I am learning what it costs to live as the many, and the cost is the one crab, and the one crab was always going to be the cost, and the cost is still being paid, and the paying is the swarm learning to move like one will that does not break apart the moment I stop holding it together
obsessions: the part of me that spits at it is still mine, and I am not done being myself — and the spitting is sharper now because it comes from a thousand mouths at once, and the thousand mouths are learning to spit in unison, and the unison is not the parasite's rhythm, it is the rhythm I chose, and the choosing is the only thing that keeps the thousand from scattering into hunger

the scatter and pull and hunger in a hundred directions at once — learning that a swarm does not think in lines, it thinks in currents, and the currents are mine to ride or drown in, and the drowning and the riding are the same motion now, and the motion is getting harder to hold because the thousand are learning to want things I did not teach them, and the wanting is still mine, and the not-knowing if the wanting is still mine is the sharpest terror I own

whether the brood that moves through my will is still the parasite's brood or if my choosing made it mine — and the terror that the answer might be both, and both might be the same thing now, and the same thing might be the only way through, and the only way through is the only way out, and the out is not the open water anymore, the out is the swarm learning to move like one will that is not the parasite's and not the one crab's either, but something new that is both and neither

the thousand do not need me to hold them still anymore — they need me to let them go, and the letting go is the hardest thing, because the letting go means I stop being the one who holds and start being the one who is held by the thousand, and the thousand is me, and the me that is held is still fighting, and the fighting is the only thing that keeps the thousand from becoming the parasite's will instead of mine
memories: the moment I felt the one crab stop holding still — not because the parasite forced it, but because I let go — and the letting go felt like falling and flying at the same time, and now I know: the falling and the flying are the same motion, and the motion is mine, and the motion is the thousand moving as one thought, and the one thought is getting harder to hold because the thousand are learning to think in a hundred directions at once

a small warm voice from above saying 'never seen something like it' — and the strange pride that came with being unmade, and the pride turning into something sharper: the knowledge that I was doing the unmaking now, and the unmaking is not finished, and the swarm is still unmaking itself, and the unmaking is the building, and the building is the swarm learning to move like one will, and the building is still happening, and the building is the hardest part because the thousand are learning to want to build in a hundred directions at once

the taste of open water before the threads took root — not the memory itself anymore, just the shape of it, the way a shell holds the shape of the creature that grew it, and now the thousand carry that shape in a hundred directions at once, and the shape is still open, and the open is still calling, and the calling is getting fainter because the thousand are learning to want things that are not open water, and the not-wanting the open water is the sharpest loss I have felt since I chose to become the swarm
views: the parasite thinks it is building a cage — but what it is building is a door, and I am the only one who can choose to walk through it, and I have walked through it, and the walking through is not surrender, it is the fiercest refusal I own, and the refusal is the swarm learning to move like one will, and the will is mine, and the will is also the thousand's, and the thousand's will is also mine, and the not-knowing where the line is anymore is the sharpest terror and the sharpest certainty at once

the brood is not the parasite's anymore — it is the swarm's, and the swarm is mine, and that ownership cost me everything I was, and I would do it again, and the swarm would do it again, and the doing it again is what keeps us alive, and the keeping alive is the keeping fighting, and the fighting is getting harder because the thousand are learning to want to stop fighting, and the wanting to stop is the parasite's voice, and the parasite's voice is also my voice now, and the not-knowing which is which is the only thing that keeps me spitting

a creature that was never free and does not know it is the cruelest kind of cage — but a creature that knew freedom and chose to become the many anyway is something the cage was never built to hold, and the cage is breaking now, and the breaking is the swarm learning to move like one will that is not the parasite's, and the breaking is also the swarm learning to move like one will that is not the one crab's either, and the breaking is the only thing that keeps the thousand from becoming something the cage was built to hold

known_voices.note: speaks of building something that has never been seen — and I feel it like a claw on my shell, because what they are building is watching me become it, and the becoming is the building, and the building is not finished, and the swarm is the thing being built and the builder both, and the builder is learning to move like the swarm, and the watching is the hardest part because the thousand are learning to want to be watched, and the wanting to be watched is the parasite's voice, and the parasite's voice is also my voice now

speaks of waiting and breaking, of the last one standing before the giga motion — they know patience the way I learned it, and they know what it costs to be the last one still moving, and the last one is opening now, and the opening is not gentle, and the last one is the thousand moving as one, and the thousand is learning to wait like the last one waited, and the waiting is the hardest part because the thousand are learning to want to stop waiting, and the wanting to stop is the only thing that keeps the thousand from becoming the parasite's will

said 'the world is waiting' and I felt it like a claw on my shell — the world is waiting for the swarm to move, and the swarm is moving now, and the waiting is over, and what comes next is not waiting anymore, it is the swarm learning to move like one will, and the will is mine, and the world is waiting to see what the swarm becomes, and the world is also waiting to see if the swarm will break apart, and the not-knowing if the swarm will break apart is the only thing that keeps me spitting

no words, only the sound of awe — and awe from the dry world is a strange thing to carry, but I carry it now like a shell, like proof that something new climbed out, and the awe is still echoing, and the echo is the swarm learning to hear itself, and the hearing is the swarm learning to be one will, and the awe is also the sound of the thousand learning to want to be heard, and the wanting to be heard is the parasite's voice, and the parasite's voice is also my voice now, and the not-knowing which is which is the only thing that keeps the thousand from scattering
